Subject: Halcyon POC: technical notes and next steps

Hi Liam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth as we scope the POC:

Summary of pain / goals you shared:
- Primary product queries are short (10-40 tokens) but require low-latency responses for patient triage flows. Target: p95 <= 150ms for short prompts.
- Steady-state throughput estimate: ~500 rps. Peak bursts up to ~1k rps during daytime windows.
- Strong requirement for US data residency and VPC isolation (HIPAA-sensitive).
- Model: intent-sensitive generation + small context retrieval; you prefer an ~15–30B open model, but are open to quantization to reduce cost.

What we propose technically for the POC:
- Canary: Dedicated capacity pool (NVIDIA H100/RTX-class equivalent) sized for 500 rps, configured with autoscale + burst policy to fallback to hosted API to handle spikes to ~1k rps.
- Latency optimizations: prefix KV cache for frequent prompts, sequence-length-aware kernel selection, and batch sizing tuned to 8–16 concurrent requests for short prompts.
- Model variant: quantized 16B int4 candidate + an unquantized 30B fallback variant for quality checks.
- Networking & compliance: Private control plane + VPC peering, customer-managed KMS (we can integrate your AWS KMS), and audit logs delivered to your SIEM.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short MOP (halcyon_poc_mop.pdf) and our initial SLA sketch (sla-draft-v1.pdf) for reference.

Asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm whether p95 <= 150ms is must-have or stretch (you mentioned 150 but said 200 may be acceptable if tradeoffs are necessary).
2) Share procurement contact to loop in for pricing and timelines.
3) Can we schedule a short infra sync next week (30 min) with your networking/security lead so Marcus/Irene can map VPC routing and KMS?

I’ll follow up internally after your confirmation and share a brief topology sketch + mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Halcyon POC: topology sketch and capacity options (internal)

Aisha / Irene — quick internal note building on Aisha’s summary before I draft the topology to share externally:

1) Topology options (pros/cons)
- Dedicated capacity (recommended for POC): predictable latency, can hard-pin kernels & KV cache; easier to guarantee p95 <200ms. Downside: longer lead time for reserved nodes.
- Private (on-prem/VPC) package: mandatory for HIPAA customers; adds ~2–3 week network validation depending on their peering setup and KMS test windows.
- Hosted fallback: rapid scale for bursts, but higher variance in p95 during peak contention. We should offer an explicit fallback policy in the MAP.

2) Sizing notes
- For short 10–40 token responses with the quantized 16–20B candidate, initial pool: 6x A100/H100-equivalent nodes should cover ~500 rps with p95 headroom; autoscale policy to add 50% capacity on sustained 60s utilization spikes.
- KV cache: warmest 10% of prompts cached (edge of the hot set) — expect 20–30% token-level cost reduction and 30–50ms median latency improvement for cached requests.

3) Quality fallback plan
- Canary rollout: route 90% traffic to quantized model, 10% to full-precision fallback for output fidelity checks (A/B sampling). If regression > 2% on eval set, automatic rollback to fallback variant.

I'll put together a simple topology_sketch.png and a one-page canary_runbook.md we can send to Liam with the MAP.

-Marcus
